question_set.question: Use focus_lines with lines equal to Age: 0, Age: 80 and use detect_anomalies with threshold equal to 2.0 and use highlight_trend with trend_type equal to increasing in order to know How do the death rate trends differ across age groups, and what significant anomalies can be observed?

answer.value: All age groups show significant declining trends in death rates over time, with the most dramatic declines in younger age groups. Age: 0 group decreased by 96.1% from 145.22 to 5.68, Age: 10 decreased by 95.6%, and Age: 25 decreased by 90.8%. Older age groups also showed substantial but slightly less dramatic declines: Age: 45 decreased by 87.7%, Age: 65 decreased by 79.2%, and Age: 80 decreased by 64.7%. Notable anomalies were detected around 1959-1961 across all age groups, with death rates spiking significantly during this period, likely reflecting historical events.

key_insights: Youngest age group (Age: 0) had the largest percentage decline at 96.1%
Oldest age group (Age: 80) consistently had the highest death rates but still declined significantly
All age groups showed anomalous spikes in death rates during 1959-1961 period
The gap between youngest and oldest death rates narrowed over time

reasoning_trace.rationale: Focus on Age: 0 and Age: 80 to compare youngest and oldest groups
Detect anomalies across all age groups to identify unusual patterns
Highlight the overall decreasing trend across all age groups
